content: I made a PR containing a proof of the Neyman-Pearson lemma, in the concrete setting from Wikipedia. I tried to adapt it to the general setting in terms of InferenceModelofMeasure. Critiques welcome.

Hi Bjorn, thanks a lot for the NP lemma PR. A few things are worth discussing:

(i) There is an earlier mathlib PR by Zixiao ( #PR reviews > #39791 NeymanPearson Lemma  ) and helpful comments on it that will be great to consider. Specifically, Remy made an important connection to a GitHub repo he has on related stuff (https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/27579), and the NP lemma can be connected to it.

(ii) NP Lemma and error of optimal testing are fundamental results that will be used in several results that are already in ongoing projects or part of future projects in preparation. It will therefore be good to discuss the version of the NP lemma we will need to develop. For example, there is a more general version that considers k+1 hypotheses and optimizes the expectation of a test function w.r.t. the k+1th hypothesis distribution under linear constraints imposed by the first k distributions (see, e.g. Theorem 3.6.1 of Lehmann & Romano, 4th Edition). It might be useful to work on the general version to decide on a roadmap.
Sounds good, so the statement in my PR could be proved as a corollary of the general result, rather than directly as I have done for now.
